title: handoff test (copy of SFTP Folder Discussion)

tldr: Fuse cannot easily take returns and goods-in ASNs in the same folder: its segmentation is tightly coupled to landing folders, so changing it would be a substantial rebuild that threatens the March go-live.
Only returns, and possibly work orders (kitting), need separating from the standard ASN flow; the same applies to the confirmation egress folders, though that is expected to be less of an issue.
Speaker 3 will go back to Edicom to ask whether returns and kitting, which come from different SAP IDOCs, can be routed to separate folders.
AS2, VAN or similar connections are not available: Fuse's SFTP service offers public key authentication only, not user and password.
Next step is Edicom's answer, then regroup if it cannot solve the routing.
decisions: Do not rebuild Fuse to split by message content for now; first try to solve the routing at the Edicom or SAP level.
Reconvene if Edicom cannot route returns and kitting to separate folders.

actions.text: Talk to Edicom about routing returns and kitting IDOCs to separate folders instead of the same ASN folder, and report back.
Raise with Edicom the SFTP connection trouble, since Fuse supports public key authentication only and not AS2, VAN or user/password, and report back.
Check whether work orders (kitting) use the same message type as returns and so also need a separate folder.
Set up a further call if needed once Edicom responds.

questions: Can Edicom route returns and kitting (work order) messages to separate folders from standard ASNs?
Do work orders use the same message type as returns, and so need splitting too?
If Edicom cannot split the folders, what is the fallback, such as a Fuse assessment or an SAP-level fix, given the March go-live?
How will Edicom connect given the key trouble, if AS2, VAN and user/password are not options?
